text:
ConocoPhillips gained 2.4% today as crude oil prices remain elevated amid competing supply concerns. The stock has climbed 12% over two weeks as global oil prices have spiked—Brent crude briefly topped $106 a barrel after a deadly attack on a Saudi airport, and a broad geopolitical risk premium persists from conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. Refiner margins have also tightened the spread between global crude ($125/barrel) and U.S. crude ($96/barrel), which favors major integrated producers like ConocoPhillips that operate both upstream and downstream assets.

The recent diplomatic moves—Trump's announced diesel deal with Russia and Republican pushback against it—add uncertainty but haven't yet resolved into lower prices. If Russian diesel does flood global markets as threatened, it could eventually pressure crude and refined product prices lower; until that materializes clearly, the geopolitical premium and supply disruption risks from the Middle East are supporting prices.
